flags.title: Slopes of 25–35° (KPKT Class III) inside the site
flags.detail: Share of site area at 25–35° on the DEM — “Parcel B (east hill)”: 2.9% of its area. Class III ground is restricted under the KPKT hill-land guidelines: development typically needs a geotechnical report and may not be approved. Treat these areas as unusable for layout until a survey and geotechnical assessment say otherwise.
flags.source: KPKT hill-land development guidelines (Garis Panduan Perancangan Pembangunan di Kawasan Bukit dan Tanah Tinggi)

flags.title: Slopes of 35° or more (KPKT Class IV) inside the site
flags.detail: Share of site area at 35° or steeper on the DEM — “Parcel B (east hill)”: 0.6% of its area. Class IV ground is generally not permitted for development under the KPKT hill-land guidelines. Exclude these areas from any usable-area or capacity estimate.
flags.source: KPKT hill-land development guidelines (Garis Panduan Perancangan Pembangunan di Kawasan Bukit dan Tanah Tinggi)

flags.title: Slopes of 15–25° (KPKT Class II) inside the site
flags.detail: Share of site area at 15–25° on the DEM — “Parcel B (east hill)”: 15.6% of its area. Under the KPKT hill-land guidelines, Class II ground is generally developable only with engineering controls such as slope protection and erosion and sediment control; expect the local authority to ask for them.
flags.source: KPKT hill-land development guidelines (Garis Panduan Perancangan Pembangunan di Kawasan Bukit dan Tanah Tinggi)

flags.title: More than 10% of site area is steeper than 10°
flags.detail: Share of site area steeper than 10° — “Parcel B (east hill)”: 42.9%. Ground this steep typically needs grading or terracing for ground-mounted PV, which adds earthworks cost and erosion-control obligations. Confirm the racking supplier's slope tolerance for the chosen mounting structure before fixing the layout.

flags.title: More than 30 m of elevation change within a site
flags.detail: Elevation range (highest minus lowest point) — “Parcel B (east hill)”: 53 m. Plan for an earthworks balance and for stormwater and erosion control designed to MSMA 2nd Edition (DID 2012) at design stage, and allow for them in early cost estimates.
flags.source: Urban Stormwater Management Manual for Malaysia (MSMA), 2nd Edition (DID 2012)

flags.title: Route gradients
flags.detail: Steepest gradient along each route, measured over at least 90 m — “33 kV cable route to PMU”: max grade 7.8% over 2.84 km (total climb 32 m). Short pitches at drains, embankments and road crossings can be steeper than a 30 m DEM shows.

flags.title: Check EIA requirements for the total area
flags.detail: Total polygon area is 60.97 ha. Whether an Environmental Impact Assessment is required depends on the activity and area categories in the schedules of the Environmental Quality (Prescribed Activities) (Environmental Impact Assessment) Order 2015, and on factors such as hill land, forest clearing or conversion of agricultural land. Have a qualified EIA consultant check the site against the current schedules.
flags.source: Environmental Quality (Prescribed Activities) (Environmental Impact Assessment) Order 2015, under the Environmental Quality Act 1974

followups.title: Licensed topographic survey
followups.detail: Before layout, earthworks or drainage design, commission a topographic survey by a licensed land surveyor (Licensed Land Surveyors Act 1958), or LiDAR / drone photogrammetry tied to surveyed ground control points.

followups.title: Geological map review (JMG)
followups.detail: Review the Jabatan Mineral dan Geosains (JMG) geological map sheet for the site: formation, lithology and any karst or ex-mining ground that affects piling, anchoring or foundations.

followups.title: Rainfall and climate data (MET Malaysia)
followups.detail: Obtain climate normals and rainfall records from the nearest MET Malaysia station; rainfall intensity feeds stormwater design to MSMA 2nd Edition.

followups.title: Surrounding land-use scan (1 / 5 / 10 km)
followups.detail: Map settlements, schools, rivers and water intakes, forest reserves, industry and mining within 1 km, 5 km and 10 km of the site as context for EIA and SIA scoping.

followups.title: Land title, zoning and local authority requirements
followups.detail: Confirm the land title, category of land use and any express conditions, the zoning in the local plan (Rancangan Tempatan), and the requirements of the local authority (PBT) for this type of development.

followups.title: Geotechnical slope assessment
followups.detail: Slopes of 25° or more were found inside the site. Commission a geotechnical assessment of slope stability before any layout or earthworks decision.

followups.title: Route wayleave and crossings
followups.detail: Confirm land access and wayleaves along the cable or access route and identify road, river and railway crossings and TNB technical requirements; none of these show on an elevation model.

caveats: Screening grade only: this is a desktop terrain screening from an open global elevation model, not a survey.

The Copernicus DEM GLO-30 is a surface model: it records the top of tree canopy and buildings, not bare ground. Plantations, forest and built-up areas read higher than the ground beneath them, and slopes at their edges can be exaggerated.
Elevations show the ground as it was in 2011–2015 (TanDEM-X acquisitions). Ponds, cuttings, platforms and buildings made since then are not represented.
The nominal 30 m resolution (analysed at about 31 m) smooths out bunds, drains and short steep cuttings, so local slopes are underestimated.
Site geometry is used exactly as supplied in the uploaded KML/KMZ file; it has not been checked against title plans or survey boundaries.
Not for authority submissions or design: planning applications, earthworks, drainage and structural design need a licensed survey and qualified engineers.
